q: Does an MVR evaporator cut emissions compared with a steam evaporator?
title: MVR evaporator vs steam evaporator
short: It replaces most of the steam with electricity: a compressor reuses the evaporated vapour as the heating medium. Scope 1 falls and Scope 2 rises. With India's grid at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, check the net change with your own steam and power figures before claiming a cut.
audience: Dairy, ZLD, sugar and chemical plants

ul: Live steam to the evaporator drops sharply.

p: Net change = steam saved multiplied by the CO2 per tonne of steam, minus extra kWh multiplied by 0.710. Rooftop or contracted renewable power improves the market-based Scope 2 result.

example.title: Worked example (illustrative)
lines: Steam saved: 10 t a day at an illustrative 0.25 t CO2 per t of steam = 2.5 t CO2
Extra electricity: 1,500 kWh a day x 0.710 = 1,065 kg, about 1.07 t CO2
Net: 2.5 minus 1.07 = about 1.4 t CO2 a day lower
example.note: Illustrative quantities only. Use your own steam factor and meter readings.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
